# A terminal for Claude Code and Codex on Windows, Linux and macOS

> Run Claude Code and Codex side by side in Paneflow. Choose the installer for your machine and set up your agents in the shell your project uses.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/blog/coding-agent-workspace-platforms

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.
     Source of truth: the paneflow.dev docs. Regenerated by
     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

Paneflow is a native terminal multiplexer for coding agents on Windows, Linux, and macOS. Run Claude Code and Codex in separate panes, follow their sessions, and review their changes beside the terminal.

The app runs locally. Your agents remain CLI processes, with their own configuration, accounts, and permissions. Paneflow is free software under GPL-3.0-or-later; access to each agent's models depends on its provider.

![Paneflow on Windows with Claude Code and Codex in terminal panes beside the integrated editor.](/images/hero-agents-dock-window.webp)

## Choose the installer for your machine

Paneflow [0.17.5](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/tag/v0.17.5) ships the following builds:

| System | Processor | Installation | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11 | x64 (`x86_64`) | [Windows installation guide](/docs/installation/windows): `.msi` | A working GPU driver with DirectX 11 feature level 10+. |
| Linux | x86_64 or ARM64 (`aarch64`) | [Linux installation guide](/docs/installation/linux): AppImage, `.deb`, `.rpm`, or `.tar.gz` | A working Vulkan driver and loader, plus the dependencies for your installation format. |
| macOS 13+ | Apple Silicon (`aarch64`) | [macOS installation guide](/docs/installation/macos): `.dmg` or Homebrew | An Apple Silicon Mac. |

This release has no native build for Intel Macs or Windows ARM. Check your processor before choosing an installer. An AppImage still needs the Linux graphics requirements listed above.

## On Windows, choose where your project runs

Use the native Windows app when your repository and tools run on Windows. Install the MSI, open Paneflow from the Start menu, and choose your shell in **Settings**. Install Claude Code or Codex in that Windows environment.

If your repository, dependencies, and agents already live in WSL2, keep them together there. The [Windows installation guide](/docs/installation/windows) explains how to run the Linux build with WSLg. Its Vulkan requirements still apply.

Installing an agent in WSL does not make it available in PowerShell, or vice versa. A WSL shell in a native Paneflow pane and the Linux app running through WSLg are two different setups. Launch the native app from the Start menu or a Windows shell.

## Launch the agents in Paneflow

Install each agent using the official [Claude Code setup guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) or [Codex CLI guide](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli). Their platform requirements and permissions apply independently of Paneflow.

1. Open a Paneflow terminal pane in your project directory.
2. Run `claude --version` or `codex --version` in that pane to check that the shell can find the agent.
3. Launch `claude` or `codex`, then follow the agent's sign-in instructions if needed.
4. Open another pane to launch the second agent.

Each pane has its own terminal session. If both agents edit the same checkout, they share its files. For independent changes, use separate [Git worktrees](/docs/worktrees), then review and integrate the branches. The [Claude Code and Codex parallel workflow](/blog/run-claude-code-and-codex-in-parallel) covers that setup.

## Review changes and return to running sessions

**Changes** compares the active checkout with `HEAD`, including staged and unstaged changes and untracked files. Open a file in **Files** to edit it, then save your corrections from the integrated editor.

When quitting Paneflow, choose **Keep sessions running** to leave the terminal processes alive. Reopening the app reconnects to them while the session host and machine remain running. A machine restart or host crash ends those processes. The [session persistence guide](/blog/keep-coding-agents-running) explains the difference between reconnecting to a live terminal and resuming an agent conversation.

## If an agent does not start

- **Paneflow cannot open a window:** check the graphics requirements in your platform's installation guide and the [troubleshooting guide](/docs/troubleshooting).
- **The shell cannot find `claude` or `codex`:** check its `PATH` and where you installed the agent, especially on Windows with WSL. Restart Paneflow after changing the agent's PATH.
- **The agent starts but cannot sign in or run a task:** check its credentials, permissions, network connection, and provider access using the agent's own documentation.

Start with one agent in your project's shell. Once it can run a task, add the second pane and choose whether the agents should share a checkout or work in separate worktrees.
